feat_rules_readme: How a bonded creature's feat pool is built. Spec section 8, D14/D15.
This file used to carry a 29-name ALLOWLIST called `feats`. It was replaced because the two
creature kinds sat at opposite extremes of one dial and neither extreme was measured: a wolf
could legally reach 167 feats and was handed 29, while an eidolon drew from the whole book
type-filtered and came back holding Prone Slinger and Opening Volley -- a sling feat and a
ranged-volley feat, on a creature with no gear.
The pool is now DERIVED and carved down, so data/feats.csv can grow without anyone editing a
list here. `creature_feat_pool()` in companion_feats.py starts from CREATURE_FEAT_TYPES and
removes, in order:
1. teamwork feats  -- the `teamwork` column. They need an ally holding the same feat.
2. racial feats    -- the `racial` column. A creature has no race to qualify with.
3. `denied_feats`  -- the residue below, which NO mechanical signal can reach.
4. `hands_required` / `language_required` -- the per-body layer, applied to the creature
actually being built rather than to the pool as a whole.
Prerequisites are still read afterwards by `legal_for_companion`, which fails CLOSED.
WHY A DENYLIST AND NOT AN ALLOWLIST. Open by default is the whole point -- a new feat is in
unless someone says no. A denylist's one real failure mode is silence, so
validate_companion_feats.py FAILS on any legally-reachable row that no rule and no list here
classifies. Nothing enters the pool unnoticed.
WHAT IS NOT HERE. Feats that merely read oddly on an animal but work -- Alertness, Animal
Affinity, Improved Unarmed Strike -- are kept. The bar is 'the creature can never use it',
not 'it is an unusual pick'. And the caster feats below are listed by hand rather than caught
by feats.py's remove_spell_caster_feats: that matcher removes Weapon Focus, whose description
carries '(or ray, if you are a spellcaster)', and keeps out Divine Defiance and Necromantic
Affinity, which a creature uses perfectly well.

hands_required_readme: The per-body layer, half one. Feats whose benefit needs a manipulator.
Every chassis species (animal, plant, vermin) is handless by construction, so this list only
ever opens for an EIDOLON that bought or was born with Limbs (Arms) -- biped and tauric base
forms have it free; aquatic, avian, quadruped and serpentine must buy it.
Weapon Finesse is deliberately NOT here: PF treats natural attacks as light weapons for it,
and it has been in the curated pool with companion_feat_changes.json coverage all along.
Armor proficiencies are NOT here either -- companions wear barding.
language_required_readme: The per-body layer, half two. Feats whose benefit needs language or trained-only mental
skills. Gated on Int 3+, the RAW line for being able to learn a language: an eidolon clears
it, an Int-2 animal companion never does.
tax_children_readme: Which feat-tax children a bonded creature may receive free. Spec section 8, D15.
The derived pool (companion_feats.creature_feat_pool) is the LEGALITY list for what a
creature picks; this is the separate, smaller
question of what feat tax may hand it. The two cannot be the same list -- tax exists to grant
the chain a primary opens, and a chain that never leaves the pool fires exactly once
But the derived chains are enormous and mostly humanoid: the old 29-name pool alone opened
children, including Drunken Brawler, Wand Dancer, Gun Twirling, Sword and Pistol and Arcane
Armor Training. A prerequisite reader cannot refuse those, because their prerequisites are
genuinely met -- an animal simply has no use for a wand. So the allowlist is curated.
Every name here is animal-appropriate AND has prerequisites companion_feats.legal_for_companion
can actually read, so nothing in this list is permanently dead: entries gated on a ki pool, a
fighter level, a skill-rank count, a deity or a size category were deliberately left out,
because the reader would refuse them on every creature forever. validate_companion_feats.py
enforces both halves. Anything refused is reported on the creature's `feat_notes`, never
